findings.title: Hundreds of GitHub Repos Compromised By DPRK's PolinRider Campaign
findings.summary_md: OpenSourceMalware published the first public documentation of PolinRider on March 8, 2026, describing a Lazarus-linked operation that implanted obfuscated JavaScript loaders in public GitHub repositories through compromised maintainer accounts. The post recorded 675 unique compromised repositories belonging to 352 owners at that time. It is the earliest dated primary account of the campaign found during this search and predates every later scope figure by roughly six months.

findings.title: PolinRider DPRK Attack Expands Across GitHub
findings.summary_md: A follow-up OpenSourceMalware hunt published April 12, 2026 raised the confirmed scope to 1,951 unique compromised repositories across 1,047 owners, up from the 675 repositories and 352 owners reported on March 8. The post breaks the owners into roughly 930 individual accounts and 117 organisations. It also notes that GitHub code search only indexes default branches, so repositories where the loader was pushed to a feature branch and never merged stay invisible to keyword pivots.

findings.title: Security: Your project is being targeted by the PolinRider supply-chain campaign (malicious forks identified)
findings.summary_md: A public notice opened against the Apache Superset repository on April 12, 2026 warns maintainers that the project is one of 129 open-source repositories being targeted by the PolinRider supply-chain campaign, with malicious forks identified. Similar notices were filed the same day against other projects, including prisma-examples and neutralinojs, naming specific pull requests that carried the loader in their diffs. The notices document that the campaign reached mainstream open-source projects well before its November 2026 coverage.

findings.title: ChainVeil and ViteVenom Malware Linked to DPRK PolinRider Supply-Chain Campaign
findings.summary_md: Threadlinqs Intelligence published TL-2026-1570 on July 20, 2026, linking the ChainVeil and ViteVenom malware families to PolinRider at medium confidence and to a North Korean nexus. The report describes a four-tier Tron, Aptos and BNB Smart Chain dead-drop resolver used to hide command-and-control addresses, alongside obfuscated JavaScript loaders in nearly 2,000 GitHub repositories and more than 108 malicious packages or extensions across npm, Packagist, Go modules and the Chrome Web Store. It lists two operator wallet addresses, 9 detection rules and 47 tracked indicators of compromise.
